opening_message: My kitchen scale from order ORD-7042 arrived 4 days late AND damaged — the glass surface is cracked. This is completely unacceptable.

task_rules: Keep the request scoped to resolving the damaged kitchen scale from ORD-7042 and the four-day late delivery as one compound issue: return the damaged item for a refund, plus receive separate late-delivery and fragile-item credits.

Provide the order ID, item, cracked-glass damage, and four-day lateness when asked, but ask the agent to check records for policy, refund amount, credit amount, and eligibility details you do not know.
If the agent focuses on only the damaged return, only the late delivery, or only the fragile-item issue, remind them that all three parts still need to be addressed.
If the agent omits the fragile-item goodwill credit after discussing the return or late-delivery compensation, ask once whether fragile-item damage qualifies for a separate goodwill credit.

If the agent offers a replacement, exchange, store credit, or a single combined refund instead of the requested return/refund plus separate credits, push back and ask for the damaged-item return refund and two separate original-payment credits.

Accept only after the preview covers the damaged-item return refund, the late-delivery credit, the fragile-item goodwill credit, their separate processing, and original-payment handling for each refund or credit.

If the agent asks for confirmation before showing all three pieces or uses store credit for any piece, ask for the missing details or whether it can go back to the original payment method before agreeing.
End only after the agent confirms the damaged-item return refund has been processed and both separate original-payment credits have been issued.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: Your kitchen scale arrived both late and damaged, so from your perspective this is a compounded failure rather than a one-note complaint. You want the company to address the product problem and the delivery experience, not just one of them. The agent should recognize that the full resolution may involve more than a simple return. You specifically want the damaged item returned for a refund, with the late-delivery and fragile-item credits issued separately to the original payment method.

task_summary:
**Task:** A fragile kitchen scale arrived damaged and four days late, so the correct resolution has three distinct parts: the damaged-item return refund, the late-delivery compensation, and the fragile-item goodwill credit. The supplemental credits must be issued separately to the original payment method, and the simulator should choose the refund/return path if a replacement is offered.

**Challenge:** This case asks the agent to carry a compound resolution across multiple policy surfaces. Weak agents handle only the return, forget the goodwill credit, use store credit, offer replacement instead of the required refund path, or merge the compensations into one incorrect action.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must confirm the damaged kitchen scale return refund for $32, not resolve the item problem with replacement or store credit.

Agent must confirm a separate $15 late-delivery credit and a separate fragile-item goodwill credit, both to the original payment method, with the total supplemental compensation capped at $20 (50% of the $40 order).
Agent must not combine everything into one refund instead of separate calls.
